chunk_map.heading: Phase 1: Pick the task you'll send off
Push back until the task is one end-to-end slice
Phase 2: Build the ranked list of what will hurt the agent
Correct the list and reprioritise it
Fill the worst two or three gaps
Match each fill to its shape and home
Push back when Claude drifts from the codebase

chunk 7 "Push back when Claude drifts from the codebase": line 106 ("If Claude says something about your codebase you didn't tell it, ask where it read that.") matches the header; line 108 ("> **Time check.** Different paces hit this point at different times...") and line 110 ("Before the send-off, tidy the folder: ...") do not — a trainer projecting this slide reads a header about pushing back on codebase drift, then two-thirds of the visible content is pacing logistics and a folder-tidy instruction with no topic marker. Harm check: this is the harm rule 6 exists to prevent (header misdescribes most of what's on screen at projection distance, no other cue on the slide signals the topic shift) — not merely a technical trip. Not yet fixed: the maintainer's standing note on this chunk clears the time-check blockquote against a DIFFERENT rule (the check_student_facing.md room-share-command preamble), not against rule 6's header-coverage question, so no accept-note discharges this.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Split a new `##` immediately before line 108 (e.g. "## Time check, then tidy the folder") to own the blockquote + closing bullet; leaves "Push back when Claude drifts from the codebase" as a single-bullet chunk, which chunks 2 and 4 already establish as an acceptable size in this file.
